section_summary: This section contains two major diplomatic files regarding Japan's cotton textile industry between August 1940 and January 1943. The first is an extensive voluntary report from the American Consulate at Osaka reviewing the 1939-1940 season, analyzing production curtailment, mounting piece goods surpluses, link system controls, and raw cotton import shifts toward Brazilian growths, supported by 17 detailed statistical tables. The second is a confidential despatch from the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires transmitting Japanese press reports on the wartime reorganization of Japan's spinning industry under a block system and the planned transfer of surplus spindles and looms to the occupied Philippines.

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter explaining the submission of original and hectograph copies of a cotton situation report by airmail.
subfiles.summary: Consul Allison explains submitting original and hectograph copies of the cotton report by airmail to meet Department of Agriculture deadlines.
subfiles.title: Airmail Transmittal of Report on Japan Cotton Situation

subfiles.about: Comprehensive voluntary economic report reviewing the 1939-1940 Japanese cotton season and analyzing the outlook for 1940-1941.
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy and Owen L. Dawson
subfiles.summary: The 1939-1940 Japanese cotton season experienced retrenchment, excessive unsold piece goods stocks, link system adjustments, and disruptions from the European war and sterling exchange collapse. For 1940-1941, raw cotton imports are projected to decline, with cheaper Brazilian cotton displacing American growths and yen-bloc cultivation unable to satisfy domestic and regional deficits. Seventeen appended statistical tables provide comprehensive data on raw cotton arrivals, mill purchases, wharf stocks, prices, yarn and cloth output, international trade balances, and staple fiber production and exports.
subfiles.title: Japan Cotton Situation - Review and Outlook

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the reorganization of Japan's cotton spinning industry under a block system and equipment transfers to occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Japanese press accounts regarding spindle curtailment under a block system and plans to transfer idle spinning and weaving equipment to the Philippines and China.
subfiles.title: Proposed Reorganization of Cotton Spinning Industry in Japan and Transfer of Equipment to the Philippines

subfiles.about: Translations of Japanese-language newspaper articles from Buenos Aires regarding Japan's textile industry reorganization, southern cotton cultivation, and Philippine spinning expansion.
subfiles.summary: Press translations reporting the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's block reorganization of spinning equipment, direct cotton planting by spinning firms in southern regions, and proposals to equip the Philippines with looms and spindles.
subfiles.title: Translations of Japanese Press Articles on Spinning Industry Reorganization and Transfer of Equipment
